pr_before.body:
The finite-clock model needs both an actual-state masslessness argument and a controlled route to a Maxwell field. This PR supplies two linked proposed theorems for the specified isotropic four-dimensional Villain law. The first derives a uniform covariance estimate on every affine integer-curl coset, including torus winding and harmonic sectors, and obtains clustering but nonsummable bounded score correlations and a gapless observable OS sector. A conservative fixed-parameter example is beta=2000, N=16384.

The second theorem is explicitly conditional on that same-delta affine estimate. An all-real-source MGF squeeze derives Gaussian joint laws, conditional lift independence transfers them to bounded physical clock scores without a volume loss, and cell-average smearing gives a Maxwell random-distribution limit locally in H^-s for s>2. The explicit electric–magnetic reflection kernel and Wick quotient yield two transverse modes with energy |p|. This stronger conclusion uses a varying-clock-order weak-coupling scaling family; it is not a dispersion claim at the first theorem's fixed parameters or a phase proof for the fixed N=3 penalty Hamiltonian. The probability law, scaling parameters and isotropic units remain supplied. Native law selection and physical identification remain open.

Validation:

- The original covariance runner and source are unchanged: 15 finite families and 18 detected faults, with their canonical cache.
- The new self-contained runner completes eight finite families and detects 26 targeted faults covering lift multiplicities, dual temperature, score and real-source signs, conditional means/noise, midpoint and cell normalization, electric–magnetic reflection/contact terms, polarization rank, dispersion, and tail/scaling constants. Direct enumeration, Fourier/image comparisons, cell quadrature and oscillatory integrals provide distinct calculation paths.
- An initial tilted-sign fault was invisible to an even variance check. An independent first-derivative check of the tilted mean now detects it. This author-check repair is documented in the source.
- Both notes include N1–N8; their canonical caches contain all five substantive N5 resolution lines. The new cache is fresh/ok with its declared 180-second timeout. New runner SHA256: `383149767aec7c7ad0f5463bf675ec2ad1221022f3e340e2da523a23cdfc76f6`.
- Vocabulary, whitespace, source/cache/N5 readiness and graph topology are checked. Relative to main `5deabeb698a27c2c3f68c5df685af2521ef15307`, the manifest adds two nodes and one dependency edge; existing entries are unchanged. The changed-evidence checker reports no failures and no existing audited rows for these new claims, which is not independent audit coverage.

The source and finite checks were reviewed personally. Finite check counts do not establish the uniform covariance theorem or continuum limit. Independent proof review of both linked notes, full pipeline, strict lint and exact combined-tree evidence validation remain landing gates. This PR proposes two bounded theorem rows; it changes no audit verdict, effective retention, axiom or approved primitive.
pr_before.title: Derive finite-clock masslessness and conditional Maxwell scaling
